reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to confirm BRAF/MEK target engagement. The combination was dosed at standard levels (GSK2118436 150mg BID, GSK1120212 2mg daily) but without PD markers we cannot confirm target modulation. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to assess MAPK pathway blockade. Cannot determine if the intended biology was achieved. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The trial achieved a 35.7% ORR (10/28 patients) in BRAF inhibitor-resistant metastatic melanoma. While the primary endpoint was marked as 'not met', a 35.7% response rate in a resistant population represents meaningful clinical activity. Additionally, 11 patients had stable disease, suggesting disease control in a substantial portion of patients. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: This was specifically in BRAF inhibitor-resistant patients, which is the appropriate population for testing combination therapy to overcome resistance. No subgroup analyses by biomarkers reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm design with small sample size (N=28) limits interpretation. No control arm to assess whether this represents improvement over standard care. The 'primary endpoint not met' designation may reflect pre-specified statistical criteria rather than lack of clinical activity.

failure_modes.evidence: No biomarker data available to assess target engagement or pathway modulation. Single-arm design without historical control comparison makes it difficult to assess true efficacy signal.
